title.zh: 卷一百三十二 列傳第八十二: 李抱玉 李抱真 王虔休 盧從史 李芃 李澄
title.en: Volume 132 Biographies 82: Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng
title.raw: 卷一百三十二 列傳第八十二: 李抱玉 李抱真 王虔休 盧從史 李芃 李澄 Volume 132 Biographies 82: Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng

sentences.zh: 李抱玉 李抱真 王虔休 盧從史 李芃李澄 族弟元素

translations.literal: Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng, and his clansman cousin Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, and Li Cheng, with the latter's clansman cousin Yuansu.

sentences.zh: 李抱玉，武德功臣安興貴之裔。

translations.literal: Li Baoyu was a descendant of An Xinggui, a meritorious official of the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu was descended from An Xinggui, one of the founding contributors of the Wude reign.

sentences.zh: 代居河西，善養名馬，為時所稱。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt in Hexi, excelled at raising famous horses, and were praised by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The family had lived in Hexi for generations, renowned for breeding fine horses.

sentences.zh: 群從兄弟，或徙居京華，習文儒，與士人通婚者，稍染士風。

translations.literal: Among the cousins, some moved to the capital, studied the literary Confucian arts, and married into scholar-official families, gradually taking on the manners of the literati.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his cousins had moved to the capital, taken up classical learning, and married into gentry families, acquiring a touch of scholarly refinement.

sentences.zh: 抱玉少長西州，好騎射，常從軍幕，沉毅有謀，小心忠謹。

translations.literal: Baoyu grew up in Xizhou, loved riding and archery, often followed military staffs, was deep and resolute with stratagems, and was careful, loyal, and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu had grown up in the western regions, loved horsemanship and archery, and spent much of his youth in army camps. He was steady and resourceful, careful, loyal, and conscientious.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，太尉李光弼引為偏裨，屢建勳績，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, Grand Marshal Li Guangbi brought him in as a junior officer; he repeatedly achieved merit and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era, Li Guangbi took him on as a subordinate officer. His repeated battlefield successes soon made his name known.

sentences.zh: 二年，自特進、右羽林軍大將軍、知軍事，遷鴻臚卿員外置同正員，持節鄭州諸軍事兼鄭州刺史、攝御史中丞、鄭陳潁亳四州節度。

translations.literal: In the second year, from Special Advancement, Grand General of the Right Yulin Army with knowledge of military affairs, he was promoted to Honglu Qing with extra appointment as regular attendant, bearing the staff as commissioner for all military affairs of Zhengzhou and concurrently Prefect of Zhengzhou, acting Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner over the four prefectures of Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he rose from special advancement and grand general of the Right Yulin Guards to Honglu Qing with full concurrent rank, commissioned for all military affairs in Zhengzhou while serving as prefect, acting censor-in-chief, and military commissioner over Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 時史思明陷洛陽，光弼守河陽，賊兵鋒方盛，光弼謂抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？

translations.literal: At that time Shi Siming had taken Luoyang; Guangbi was defending Heyang while the rebel spearhead was at its height. Guangbi said to Baoyu, "General, can you hold the south city for me for two days?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming had seized Luoyang, and Guangbi was holding Heyang against a rebel force at the height of its power. He asked Baoyu, "Can you hold the south wall for me for two days?

sentences.zh: 」抱玉曰：「過期若何？

translations.literal: " Baoyu said, "What if the deadline passes?
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyu asked, "What if two days pass and relief has not come?

sentences.zh: 」光弼曰：「過期而救不至，任棄城也。

translations.literal: " Guangbi said, "If the deadline passes and relief does not arrive, you may abandon the city as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangbi replied, "If relief has not arrived by then, you may abandon the city at your discretion.

sentences.zh: 」賊帥周摯領安太清、徐黃玉等先次南城，將陷之，抱玉乃紿之曰：「吾糧盡，明日當降。

translations.literal: " The rebel commander Zhou Zhi, leading An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, first encamped at the south city and was about to take it. Baoyu then deceived them, saying, "Our grain is exhausted; tomorrow we shall surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Rebel commander Zhou Zhi, with An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, camped first at the south wall and was poised to storm it. Baoyu deceived them: "Our provisions are gone—we will surrender tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」賊眾大喜，斂軍以俟之。

translations.literal: " The rebel troops were greatly pleased and drew in their forces to wait.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels were delighted and held their army back to wait.

sentences.zh: 抱玉因得繕完設備，明日，堅壁請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu thereby was able to repair and complete his defenses; the next day he shut the walls tight and offered battle.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu used the respite to repair his defenses. The next day he shut the gates and challenged them to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊怒欺紿，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels, enraged at being deceived, pressed the attack fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at having been tricked, the rebels assaulted the wall at once.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵，表裡夾攻，殺傷甚眾，摯軍退。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent out surprise troops and attacked from inside and outside; many were killed and wounded, and Zhi's army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent out ambush forces to strike them from front and rear. Casualties were heavy, and Zhou Zhi's army fell back.

sentences.zh: 光弼自將於中氵單城，摯舍南城攻中氵單，不勝，乃整軍將攻北城。

translations.literal: Guangbi himself commanded at Zhongtan city; Zhi abandoned the south city to attack Zhongtan, was unsuccessful, and then reorganized his army to attack the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi took command at Zhongtan. Zhou Zhi left the south wall and assaulted Zhongtan without success, then re-formed his troops to strike the north wall.

sentences.zh: 光弼以兵出戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Guangbi led his troops out to battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi marched out and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 固河陽，復懷州，皆功居第一，遷澤州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In securing Heyang and recovering Huaizhou, his merit ranked first in each case; he was promoted to Prefect of Zezhou and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in merit for holding Heyang and recovering Huaizhou, and was promoted to prefect of Zezhou with concurrent rank as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，擢為澤潞節度使、潞州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫，加領陳、鄭二州，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Baoyu was promoted to military commissioner of Zelu, chief administrator of the Lu prefectural metropolitan area, and concurrent Grand Censor, with added charge of Chen and Zheng prefectures, and was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Daizong's accession he was made military commissioner of Zelu, chief administrator at Lu prefecture, and grand censor, with added authority over Chen and Zheng, and was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 抱玉上言：「臣貫屬涼州，本姓安氏，以祿山構禍，恥與同姓，去至德二年五月，蒙恩賜姓李氏，今請割貫屬京兆府長安縣。

translations.literal: Baoyu submitted a memorial: "Your servant's registered domicile is Liangzhou; my original surname was An. Because An Lushan brought calamity, I was ashamed to share that surname. In the fifth month of the second year of Zhide I received the grace of being granted the surname Li. I now request that my registered domicile be transferred to Chang'an county in Jingzhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu memorialized the throne: "I was registered in Liangzhou and bore the surname An. After An Lushan's rebellion I was ashamed to share that name, and in the fifth month of Zhide 2 I was honored with the imperial surname Li. I now ask that my registration be transferred to Chang'an county in the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」許之，因是舉宗並賜國姓。

translations.literal: " The request was granted, and thereby the whole clan was granted the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted, and his entire clan received the imperial surname as well.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年冬，吐蕃寇京師，乘輿幸陝，諸軍潰卒及村閭亡命相聚為盜，京城南面子午等五穀群盜頗害居人，朝廷遣薛景仙領兵為五穀使招討，連月不捷，乃詔抱玉兼鳳翔節度使討之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangde, Tibetans raided the capital; the imperial carriage went to Shan. Routed soldiers of various armies and village fugitives gathered as bandits. South of the capital, in the Five Valleys of Ziwu and elsewhere, bandit gangs greatly harmed the inhabitants. The court sent Xue Jingxian to lead troops as commissioner for the Five Valleys to suppress them; for months he had no success, and Baoyu was then ordered as concurrent Fengxiang military commissioner to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Tibetan forces threatened the capital and the emperor withdrew to Shan. Demobilized troops and village outlaws banded together as robbers. South of Chang'an, in the Five Valleys including Ziwu, gangs preyed heavily on the populace. Xue Jingxian was sent as Five Valleys commissioner to suppress them, but after months had achieved nothing. Baoyu was then ordered to take concurrent command at Fengxiang and finish the campaign.

sentences.zh: 抱玉探知賊帥行止之處，先分屯諸谷，乃設奇潛使輕銳數百南自洋州入攻之。

translations.literal: Baoyu learned where the bandit chiefs were moving, first stationed detachments in the various valleys, then set an ambush and secretly sent several hundred light elite troops south from Yangzhou to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: After locating the bandit leaders, he posted troops in the valleys and sent several hundred picked light infantry south from Yang prefecture in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高玉方與諸偷會，遽為銳卒數十人掩擒之，因大搜獲偷黨，悉斬之，餘黨不討自潰，旬日內五穀平。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gao Yu was just meeting with the various thieves when several dozen elite troops suddenly seized him in an ambush; a great search then captured the thief bands, all were beheaded, the remaining factions collapsed without further campaigning, and within ten days the Five Valleys were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Gao Yu was conferring with his fellow bandits when a few dozen elite soldiers seized him by surprise. A sweep captured the rest of the gangs, who were all executed. The remaining bands melted away without a fight, and the Five Valleys were pacified within ten days.

sentences.zh: 以功遷司空，余並如故。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to Minister of Works; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to minister of works; his other offices were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃每歲犯境，上以岐陽國之西門，寄在抱玉，恩寵無比，遷同中書門下平章事，又兼山南西道節度使、河西隴右山南西道副元帥、判梁州事，連統三道節制，兼領鳳翔、潞、梁三大府，秩處三公。

translations.literal: At that time Tibetans raided the borders every year; the emperor regarded Qiyang as the western gate of the realm and entrusted it to Baoyu with favor beyond compare. He was promoted to Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and concurrently military commissioner of Southwest Shannan, deputy commander-in-chief of Hexi, Longyou, and Southwest Shannan, with authority over Liangzhou, commanding three circuits in succession and concurrently heading the three great prefectures of Fengxiang, Lu, and Liang, ranking with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided the frontier every year, and the emperor treated Qiyang as the realm's western gate, entrusting it to Baoyu with unparalleled favor. He rose to associate grand councilor, concurrently commanded Southwest Shannan, served as deputy commander-in-chief over Hexi, Longyou, and Southwest Shannan, and governed Liangzhou—holding three circuits at once and the great prefectures of Fengxiang, Lu, and Liang, with rank equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 抱玉以任位崇重，抗疏懇讓司空及山南西道節度、判梁州事，乞退授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baoyu, because his duties and rank were so exalted, submitted a forthright memorial earnestly declining the post of Minister of Works, the Southwest Shannan military commission, and authority over Liangzhou, and begged to step back to the post of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his offices too weighty, Baoyu memorialized earnestly to decline the ministry of works, the Southwest Shannan commission, and authority over Liangzhou, asking instead to return to the post of minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其謙讓，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his modesty and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his humility and agreed.

sentences.zh: 抱雲凡鎮鳳翔十餘年，雖無破虜之功，而禁暴安人，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Baoyu governed Fengxiang for more than ten years in all; though he had no merit in defeating foreign invaders, in restraining violence and settling the people he was much praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu held Fengxiang for more than ten years. He won no great victories over foreign foes, but in suppressing violence and keeping the peace he earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 大曆十二年卒，上甚悼之，輟朝三日，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dali he died; the emperor grieved deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Dali. The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 李抱真，抱玉從父弟也。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen was Baoyu's younger cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen was Baoyu's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 抱玉為澤潞節度使，甚器抱真，任以軍事，累授汾州別駕。

translations.literal: When Baoyu was military commissioner of Zelu, he greatly valued Baozhen, entrusted him with military affairs, and repeatedly appointed him vice-prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyu commanded Zelu, he prized Baozhen highly, put him in charge of military affairs, and repeatedly appointed him vice-prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，僕固懷恩反於汾州，抱真陷焉，乃脫身歸京師。

translations.literal: At that time Pugu Huai'en rebelled at Fenzhou; Baozhen was caught up in it but escaped and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled at Fenzhou, Baozhen was trapped in the uprising but slipped away and made his way back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗以懷恩倚回紇，所將朔方兵又勁，憂甚，召見抱真問狀，因奏曰：「郭子儀領朔方之眾，人多思之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong, because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and the Shuofang troops he led were also formidable, was deeply worried. He summoned Baozhen to inquire about the situation, and Baozhen memorialized: "Guo Ziyi once commanded the Shuofang forces, and the men still long for him.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was deeply alarmed: Huai'en had Uyghur support and commanded the formidable Shuofang army. He summoned Baozhen for a briefing. Baozhen said, "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang troops, and the men still miss him.

sentences.zh: 懷恩欺其眾，曰『子儀為朝恩所殺』，詐而用之。

translations.literal: Huai'en deceives the troops, saying 'Ziyi was killed by court favoritism,' and uses them by fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en has deceived them with the lie that 'Ziyi was murdered by court intrigue,' and leads them on that pretense.

sentences.zh: 今復子儀之位，可不戰而克。

translations.literal: If Ziyi's post is now restored, the enemy can be overcome without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Restore Ziyi to command, and the rebellion can be broken without a battle.

sentences.zh: 」其後懷恩子瑒為其下所殺，懷恩奔遁，多如抱真策，因是遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Huai'en's son Chang was killed by his subordinates, and Huai'en fled in flight; events largely followed Baozhen's plan, and for this he was promoted to Vice-Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Huai'en's son Chang was soon killed by his own men, and Huai'en fled—much as Baozhen had predicted. Baozhen was promoted to vice-director of the palace service.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，為陳鄭、澤潞節度留後，抱真因中謝言曰：「臣雖無可取，當今百姓勞逸，系在牧守，願得一郡以自試。

translations.literal: Before long he became acting commissioner of the Chen-Zheng and Zelu circuits. At his audience of thanks Baozhen said, "Though your servant has little to offer, the people's toil and ease today depend on their governors; I wish to receive one prefecture to prove myself.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became acting commissioner of Chen-Zheng and Zelu. At his audience of thanks he said, "I have little to boast of, but the people's welfare depends on their prefects. Grant me one command so I may prove myself.

sentences.zh: 」上許之，改授澤州刺史，兼為澤潞節度副使。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted this and transferred him to Prefect of Zezhou, concurrently as deputy military commissioner of Zelu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and appointed him prefect of Zezhou, with concurrent rank as deputy commissioner of Zelu.

sentences.zh: 居二年，轉懷州刺史，復為懷澤潞觀察使留後，凡八年。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to Prefect of Huaizhou and again served as acting observation commissioner of Huai-Zelu; in all this lasted eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became prefect of Huaizhou and again served as acting observation commissioner of Huai-Zelu—a total of eight years in those roles.

sentences.zh: 抱玉卒，抱真仍領留後。

translations.literal: When Baoyu died, Baozhen continued to hold the acting commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyu's death, Baozhen remained as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 抱真密揣山東當有變，上黨且當兵沖，是時乘戰余之地，土瘠賦重，人益困，無以養軍士。

translations.literal: Baozhen secretly judged that Shandong would soon see upheaval and that Shangdang would become a military choke point. The region had been worn by war; the soil was poor and taxes heavy, the people grew ever more distressed, and there was no means to maintain the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen sensed that trouble was brewing in the east and that Shangdang would become a strategic battleground. The land was war-ravaged, the soil poor and taxes crushing; the people were exhausted and there was no money to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 籍戶丁男，三選其一，有材力者免其租徭，給弓矢，令之曰：「農之隙，則分曹角射；

translations.literal: He registered household adult males, chose one in three, exempted the able-bodied from rent and corvée, supplied bows and arrows, and ordered them: "In the intervals of farming, divide into groups and compete in archery;
translations.idiomatic: He registered every adult male in the households, selected one man in three, exempted the able-bodied from taxes and corvée, issued bows and arrows, and ordered: "Between planting seasons, divide into squads and compete at archery;

sentences.zh: 歲終，吾當會試。

translations.literal: at year's end I shall hold a general examination.
translations.idiomatic: at year's end I will hold a general review.

sentences.zh: 」及期，按簿而征之，都試以示賞罰，覆命之如初。

translations.literal: " When the time came, he summoned them according to the registers, held a collective examination to show rewards and punishments, and reissued the orders as before.
translations.idiomatic: " When the time came he called them up by the register, held a mass review with rewards and penalties, and renewed the standing orders.

sentences.zh: 比三年，則皆善射，抱真曰：「軍可用矣。

translations.literal: Within three years they were all skilled archers. Baozhen said, "The army is ready for use.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they were all expert archers. Baozhen said, "The army is ready.

sentences.zh: 」於是舉部內鄉兵，得成卒二萬，前既不廩費，府庫益實，乃繕甲兵，為戰具，遂雄視山東。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised the local militia throughout his jurisdiction and obtained twenty thousand trained soldiers. Because he had not spent on grain rations before, the treasury grew fuller; he then repaired armor and weapons, prepared war equipment, and came to dominate Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: " He then mobilized the local militia and fielded twenty thousand trained soldiers. Having spent nothing on rations, his treasury grew flush. He outfitted them with armor and weapons and came to dominate the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下稱昭義軍步兵冠諸軍。

translations.literal: At that time the realm acclaimed the infantry of the Zhaoyi army as foremost among all forces.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Zhaoyi infantry were considered the finest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 無幾，復代李承昭為昭義軍及磁邢節度觀察留後，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he again replaced Li Chengzhao as acting military and observation commissioner of the Zhaoyi army and the Ci-Xing circuits, and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he succeeded Li Chengzhao as acting commissioner of the Zhaoyi army and the Ci-Xing circuits, with additional rank as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，拜檢校工部尚書，兼潞州長史、昭義軍節度支度營田、澤潞磁邢觀察使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Baozhen was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Chief Administrator of Luzhou, commissioner for supplies, farming, and finance of the Zhaoyi army, and observation commissioner of Zelu, Ci, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Baozhen was made acting minister of works, chief administrator of Luzhou, commissioner for supplies and farming of the Zhaoyi army, and observation commissioner over Zelu, Ci, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，田悅以魏博反，乃悉兵圍邢州及臨洺益急，詔河東節度使馬燧及神策兵救之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Tian Yue rebelled with Weibo and mustered all his troops to besiege Xingzhou and Linming with growing urgency; the court ordered Ma Sui, military commissioner of Hedong, and the Shence troops to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2, Tian Yue rebelled from Weibo and threw his full strength against Xingzhou and Linming. Ma Sui of Hedong and the Shence army were ordered to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 抱真與燧敗悅兵於雙岡，斬悅將楊朝光，又擊破悅於臨洺，遂解臨洺及邢州之圍，以功加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baozhen and Sui defeated Yue's troops at Shuanggang, beheaded Yue's general Yang Chaoguang, and again routed Yue at Linming, thereby lifting the sieges of Linming and Xingzhou; for this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen and Ma Sui defeated Tian Yue at Shuanggang and beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, then routed him again at Linming and lifted both sieges. Baozhen was promoted to acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 復與燧大破悅於洹水，悅以數百騎走歸魏州。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he inflicted a great defeat on Yue at the Huan River; Yue fled with several hundred horsemen back to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Ma Sui he again crushed Tian Yue on the Huan River; Yue fled to Weizhou with a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 復與燧圍魏州，又敗悅於城下，以功加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he besieged Weizhou and once more defeated Yue below the walls; for this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Weizhou together and defeated Yue again beneath the walls. Baozhen was promoted to acting right vice director.

sentences.zh: 時悅窘蹙，硃滔、王武俊皆反，聯兵救悅，抱真與燧等退次魏縣。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was hard pressed; Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun both rebelled and joined forces to rescue Yue; Baozhen and Sui and the others withdrew and encamped at Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was cornered, but Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun also rebelled and marched to his relief. Baozhen, Ma Sui, and the others fell back to Weixian.

sentences.zh: 上幸奉天，中使告問至，諸將皆仰天慟哭。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Fengtian; when the palace envoy arrived with news, all the generals looked up to heaven and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withdrew to Fengtian. When the palace envoy brought word, the generals looked to heaven and wept.

sentences.zh: 李懷光席捲奔命，馬燧、李芃各引兵歸鎮。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang swept off in haste; Ma Sui and Li Peng each led their troops back to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang rushed away; Ma Sui and Li Peng each marched their armies home.

sentences.zh: 硃泚既汙宮闕，時李希烈陷大梁，李納亦反鄆州。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had already defiled the palace precincts; at that time Li Xilie had taken Daliang, and Li Na also rebelled at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had seized the capital; Li Xilie held Daliang, and Li Na rebelled at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 無何，上幸梁州，李懷光又竊據河中。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor went to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang again seized Hedong by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang seized Hedong as well.

sentences.zh: 抱真獨於擾攘傾潰之中，以山東三州外抗群賊，內輯軍士，群賊深憚之。

translations.literal: Baozhen alone amid turmoil and collapse held the three Shandong prefectures, resisted the rebel hosts from without, and kept his soldiers in order within; the rebel bands deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Amid universal turmoil Baozhen alone held three eastern prefectures, held off the rebel hosts from without, and kept discipline within. The rebels feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 興元初，遷檢校左僕射、平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he was promoted to acting left vice director and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時硃滔悉幽薊軍，借兵回紇，擁眾五萬，南向以應泚，攻圍貝州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao mustered all the You-Ji armies, borrowed Uyghur troops, and with a host of fifty thousand marched south to support Ci and besieged Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao mobilized the entire You-Ji army, borrowed Uyghur auxiliaries, and marched south with fifty thousand men to support Zhu Ci, besieging Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，群賊附於希烈，希烈僭偽，有臣屬群賊意，群心稍離。

translations.literal: At first the rebel bands had attached themselves to Xilie; when Xilie usurped the throne, he treated the other rebels as subjects, and their hearts gradually turned away.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders had initially rallied to Li Xilie, but when he declared himself emperor and treated them as vassals, their loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 上自奉天下罪己之詔，悉赦群賊，抱真乃遣門客賈林以大義說武俊，合從擊硃滔，武俊許之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued from Fengtian an edict blaming himself and pardoning all the rebel bands. Baozhen then sent his retainer Jia Lin to persuade Wujun on grounds of righteousness to join in attacking Zhu Tao; Wujun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: From Fengtian the emperor issued a self-reproach edict pardoning all rebels. Baozhen sent his retainer Jia Lin to persuade Wang Wujun on principle to join against Zhu Tao, and Wujun agreed.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍尚相疑，抱真乃以數騎徑入武俊營。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies still mistrusted each other; Baozhen therefore rode with only a few horsemen straight into Wujun's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies still distrusted each other, so Baozhen rode into Wang Wujun's camp with only a handful of escorts.

sentences.zh: 其將去也，賓客皆止之，抱真遣軍司馬盧玄卿勒軍部分曰：「僕今日此舉，系天下安危。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, his guests all tried to stop him. Baozhen sent his army marshal Lu Xuanqing to muster the troops and divide the commands, saying, "My action today bears on the safety of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His staff tried to stop him, but Baozhen sent his army marshal Lu Xuanqing to array the troops and said, "What I do today concerns the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 僕死不還，領軍事以聽朝命，亦唯子；

translations.literal: If I die and do not return, take command of the army and await the court's orders—that too rests with you alone;
translations.idiomatic: If I do not return, take command and await the court's orders—that is also yours alone;

sentences.zh: 奮勵士馬，東向雪僕之恥，亦唯子。

translations.literal: to rouse the soldiers and horses and march east to wipe away my disgrace—that too rests with you alone."
translations.idiomatic: to rouse the troops and march east to avenge my death—that too is yours alone."

sentences.zh: 」言訖而去。

translations.literal: " Having spoken, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he rode off.

sentences.zh: 武俊設備甚嚴，抱真曰：「硃泚、希烈僭竊大位，硃滔攻圍貝州，此輩皆欲陵駕吾屬。

translations.literal: Wujun had made his guard very strict. Baozhen said, "Zhu Ci and Xilie have usurped the throne; Zhu Tao is besieging Beizhou—these men all wish to tower over us.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun's camp was on full alert. Baozhen said, "Zhu Ci and Li Xilie have seized the throne; Zhu Tao is besieging Beizhou. They mean to dominate us all.

sentences.zh: 足下既不能自振數賊之上，舍九葉天子而北面臣反虜乎？

translations.literal: If you cannot raise yourself above these several rebels, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and turn north to serve rebel usurpers as your lord?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot stand above these rebels, will you abandon the emperor of nine generations and bow north to serve traitors?

sentences.zh: 乃者聖上奉天下罪己之詔，可謂禹、湯之主也。

translations.literal: Just now the sage emperor issued from Fengtian an edict blaming himself—he may be called a ruler in the mold of Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has just issued a self-reproach edict from Fengtian—a ruler in the mold of Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 」因言及播越，持武俊哭，涕泗交下，武俊亦哭，感動左右。

translations.literal: " Speaking then of the emperor's exile, he seized Wujun and wept; tears and mucus streamed down. Wujun wept too, moving all those present.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke of the emperor's flight from the capital, seized Wang Wujun, and wept until tears streamed down both their faces, moving everyone present.

sentences.zh: 因退臥武俊帳中，酣寢久之。

translations.literal: He then withdrew and lay down to sleep in Wujun's tent, sleeping soundly for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired to Wang Wujun's tent and slept soundly for a long time.

sentences.zh: 武俊感其不疑，待之益恭，指心仰天曰：「此身已許公死敵矣。

translations.literal: Wujun, moved by his lack of suspicion, treated him with still greater respect, pointed to his heart and looked up to heaven, saying, "This body is already pledged to die as your enemy's foe.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by such trust, Wang Wujun treated him with even greater respect, pointed to his heart, and said to heaven, "I have pledged this life to fight your enemies unto death.

sentences.zh: 」遂與結為兄弟而別，約明日合戰，遂擊破硃滔於經城，以功加檢校司空，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: " They then swore brotherhood and parted, agreeing to join battle the next day; they thereupon routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng. For this merit he was given the additional post of Acting Minister of Works with a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " They swore brotherhood and parted, agreeing to fight together the next day. They routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng, and Baozhen was promoted to acting minister of works with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，朝於京師，居頃之，還鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he attended court in the capital; after a short stay he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he went to court; after a brief stay he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 抱真沉斷多智計，嘗欲招致天下賢俊，聞人之善，必令持貨幣數千里邀致之；

translations.literal: Baozhen was deep, resolute, and full of stratagems; he once wished to gather worthy men from across the realm. When he heard of someone's excellence, he always sent men bearing goods for thousands of li to invite them;
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was shrewd and resourceful. He wished to gather talented men from across the empire; whenever he heard of someone's merit, he sent agents bearing gifts for thousands of miles to invite them.

sentences.zh: 至與語無可採者，漸退之。

translations.literal: when he spoke with them and found nothing worth taking, he gradually sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: If conversation revealed nothing worthwhile, he quietly let them go.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，乃大起台榭，穿池沼以自娛。

translations.literal: When the realm was at peace he greatly raised terraces and pavilions and dug ponds for his own amusement.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was at peace he built grand pavilions and dug ornamental ponds for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 晚節又好方士，以冀長生。

translations.literal: In his later years he also favored alchemical masters, hoping for long life.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he also turned to Daoist adepts, hoping for immortality.

sentences.zh: 有孫季長者，為抱真練金丹，紿抱真曰：「服之當升仙」遂署為賓僚。

translations.literal: There was one Sun Jichang, who refined golden elixir pills for Baozhen and deceived him, saying, "If you take them you will ascend as an immortal," whereupon he was appointed to the staff of guests and aides.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixir pills for him and promised that taking them would bring immortality. Baozhen made him a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 數謂參佐曰：「此丹秦皇、漢武皆不能得，唯我遇之，他年朝上清，不復偶公輩矣。

translations.literal: He often told his aides, "This elixir neither the First Emperor of Qin nor Emperor Wu of Han could obtain; only I have encountered it. In years to come I shall ascend to the Upper Clarity and no longer keep company with the likes of you.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his staff, "Neither the First Emperor nor Han Wudi could obtain this elixir—only I have been granted it. One day I shall ascend to the heavens and leave your company behind.

sentences.zh: 」復夢駕鶴衝天，寤而刻木鶴、衣道士衣以習乘之。

translations.literal: " He also dreamed of riding a crane soaring to heaven; on waking he carved a wooden crane, put on a Daoist priest's robe, and practiced mounting it.
translations.idiomatic: " He dreamed of riding a crane into the sky. On waking he carved a wooden crane, donned a Daoist robe, and practiced mounting it.

sentences.zh: 凡服丹二萬丸，腹堅不食，將死，不知人者數日矣。

translations.literal: In all he took twenty thousand pills; his belly grew hard and he would not eat. As death approached he did not recognize people for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed twenty thousand pills until his belly hardened and he stopped eating. Near death he was unresponsive for days.

sentences.zh: 道士牛洞玄以豬肪谷漆下之，殆盡。

translations.literal: The Daoist priest Niu Dongxuan used pork fat and grain lacquer to purge him, and nearly brought it all up.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Niu Dongxuan purged him with pork fat and grain lacquer until he had nearly voided everything.

sentences.zh: 病少間，季長復曰：「垂上仙，何自棄也！

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, Jichang again said, "You are on the verge of ascending as an immortal—why abandon it yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When he rallied slightly, Jichang said again, "You are on the verge of immortality—why throw that away?

sentences.zh: 」益服三千丸，頃之卒。

translations.literal: " He took three thousand more pills and shortly thereafter died.
translations.idiomatic: " He took three thousand more pills and soon died.

sentences.zh: 初，抱真久疾，好礻幾祥，或令厭勝，為巫祝所惑，請降官爵以禳除之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Baozhen had long been ill, he favored sacrificial divination and sometimes ordered exorcistic rites; deluded by shamans and prayer-masters, he requested to lower his rank and titles to avert calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during his long illness, he had turned to divination and exorcism and, swayed by shamans, asked to reduce his rank and titles to ward off misfortune.

sentences.zh: 是年，凡七上章讓司空，復為檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: That year he submitted seven memorials in all declining the post of Minister of Works and was again made Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: That year he memorialized seven times to decline the ministry of works and was restored to acting left vice director.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年卒，時年六十二，廢朝三日，贈太保，賻以布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died at the age of sixty-two; court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor, and condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were given in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Zhenyuan at sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days, he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor, and graded gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were sent to his family.

sentences.zh: 抱真薨之日，其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪不發。

translations.literal: On the day Baozhen died, his son, Palace Attendant Censor Jian, concealed the death and did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Baozhen died, his son Jian, a palace attendant censor, concealed the death and did not announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 營田副使盧會昌令抱真從甥元仲經潛與緘謀，其明日，將吏會集，仲經詐為抱真令曰：「吾疾甚，不能蒞職，今令緘掌軍事，諸軍善佐之。

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner for farming Lu Huichang had Baozhen's cousin Yuan Zhongjing secretly plot with Jian. The next day, when the generals and officials assembled, Zhongjing falsely issued orders in Baozhen's name, saying, "My illness is severe and I cannot attend to duty; I now order Jian to take command of the army—let all the forces support him well.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy farming commissioner Lu Huichang had Baozhen's cousin Yuan Zhongjing plot secretly with Jian. The next day, when officers assembled, Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "I am gravely ill and cannot command. Jian will take military affairs—support him well.

sentences.zh: 」節度副使李說及諸將吏俯首，皆曰：「諾」。

translations.literal: " Deputy military commissioner Li Shuo and all the generals and officials bowed their heads and said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " Deputy commissioner Li Shuo and the other officers bowed and assented.

sentences.zh: 須臾，緘盛服而出，眾皆拜之，緘乃悉府藏頒賞軍士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jian came out in full ceremonial dress; all bowed to him, and Jian then distributed the entire treasury stores as rewards to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Jian appeared in full dress. All bowed to him, and he distributed the entire treasury to the troops as reward.

sentences.zh: 盧會昌仍詐為抱真表，請以職事付緘。

translations.literal: Lu Huichang again forged a memorial in Baozhen's name requesting that official duties be entrusted to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huichang forged another memorial in Baozhen's name asking that command be transferred to Jian.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又令諸將連奏請緘領軍。

translations.literal: The next day he again had the generals submit joint memorials requesting that Jian take command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he had the generals submit joint memorials asking that Jian take command.

sentences.zh: 上已聞真疾病，請見明日。

translations.literal: The emperor had already heard that Baozhen was ill and had requested an audience for the next day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already heard Baozhen was ill and had summoned him to court the next day.

sentences.zh: 如此者凡三日，緘乃出造中使，左右皆陳兵，甚嚴備。

translations.literal: This went on for three days in all; then Jian went out to visit the palace envoy, with troops drawn up on both sides in very strict array.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for three days. Then Jian went out to meet the palace envoy with armed escorts drawn up on every side.

sentences.zh: 中使謂緘曰：「朝廷已知相公薨歿，令以兵務屬延貴，侍御宜歸發喪行服也。

translations.literal: The palace envoy said to Jian, "The court already knows that the lord commissioner has died and has ordered that military affairs be assigned to Yanguai. Attendant Censor, you should return home to announce the mourning and observe the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy told Jian, "The court already knows your father is dead and has assigned military affairs to Yanguai. You should go home, announce the death, and observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 」緘愕然，出謂諸將曰：「有詔不許緘掌事，諸公意若何？

translations.literal: " Jian was startled; he went out and said to the generals, "There is an edict forbidding Jian to take command—what do you gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: " Jian was stunned. He went out and asked the generals, "The court forbids me to take command—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」將吏莫有對者。

translations.literal: " None of the generals and officials replied.
translations.idiomatic: " No one answered.

sentences.zh: 緘懼而退，遽以使印及管鑰歸監軍。

translations.literal: Jian, fearful, withdrew and hastily returned the commissioner seal and the keys to the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Jian withdrew and immediately returned the seal and keys to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 是日，乃發喪，畢一哭。

translations.literal: That same day they announced the mourning and completed the first wailing.
translations.idiomatic: That day they announced the death and held the first mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 中使召延貴，以口詔令視事，趣遣緘赴東都。

translations.literal: The palace envoy summoned Yanguai and by oral edict ordered him to take charge of affairs, urging Jian to proceed to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy summoned Yanguai and by oral edict put him in command, ordering Jian to proceed to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 元仲經逃於外，延貴捕得殺之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongjing had fled outside; Yanguai captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongjing had fled; Yanguai captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 既歸罪仲經，盧會昌得不坐。

translations.literal: Once guilt was laid on Zhongjing, Lu Huichang was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: With blame fixed on Zhongjing, Lu Huichang escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 緘初謀亂，遣裨將陳榮詐以文書告成德節度使王武俊，求假財帛，武俊大怒曰：「吾與汝府公善者，冀恭王命，非同惡也。

translations.literal: When Jian first plotted rebellion, he sent his junior officer Chen Rong with a forged document to inform Wang Wujun, military commissioner of Chengde, requesting borrowed funds and goods. Wujun was greatly angered and said, "I was on good terms with your lord commissioner, hoping to honor the royal command together—we were not fellow evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: In his plot Jian had sent Chen Rong with a forged letter to Wang Wujun of Chengde asking for money and supplies. Wujun was furious: "Your father and I were allies in serving the throne—we were never partners in treason.

sentences.zh: 今聞已亡，孰詐令其子而不俟朝旨耶？

translations.literal: Now I hear he is dead—who has deceived his son into acting without awaiting the court's command?
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear he is dead—who has tricked his son into seizing command without waiting for the court?

sentences.zh: 何敢告我，況有求也！

translations.literal: How dare he inform me—and moreover make a request!
translations.idiomatic: How dare he come to me—and ask for favors besides!

sentences.zh: 」乃囚陳榮而遣使讓緘焉。

translations.literal: " He then imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to rebuke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: " He imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to rebuke Jian.

sentences.zh: 王虔休，字君佐，汝州梁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu, courtesy name Junzuo, was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu, courtesy name Junzuo, was from Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 本名延貴。

translations.literal: His original name was Yanguai.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yanguai.

sentences.zh: 少涉獵書籍，鄉里間以信義畏慕之，尤好武藝。

translations.literal: In youth he dipped into books; in his home district people feared and admired him for faith and righteousness, and he especially loved martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read widely. Neighbors respected him for integrity and admired his martial skill.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，汝州刺史李深用之為將。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, Li Shen, Prefect of Ruzhou, employed him as a general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era, Prefect Li Shen of Ruzhou employed him as an officer.

sentences.zh: 久之，澤潞節度李抱真聞名，厚以財帛招之，累授兵馬使押衙。

translations.literal: After some time Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Zelu, heard of his fame and recruited him with generous gifts of goods and silk, repeatedly appointing him army horse commissioner and yamen escort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen of Zelu heard of him and recruited him with rich gifts, appointing him repeatedly as army horse commissioner and headquarters escort.

sentences.zh: 建中初，抱真統兵馬與諸將征討河北，其雙岡、水寨營等陣，虔休攻戰居多，擢為步軍都虞候，累加兼御史中丞、大夫，賜實封百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Baozhen led the army and cavalry with the generals to campaign in Hebei; at the battles of Shuanggang, the water-fort camps, and the like, Qianxiu fought in the majority of assaults. He was promoted to chief adjutant of the infantry, repeatedly given concurrent posts as Censor-in-Chief and Grand Censor, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Baozhen led the army against Hebei. Qianxiu fought in most of the major engagements at Shuanggang and the water forts. He was promoted to chief infantry adjutant, given concurrent rank as censor-in-chief and grand censor, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 洎抱真卒，裨將元仲經等議立抱真子緘，軍中擾亂，虔休正色言於眾曰：「軍州是天子軍州，將帥闕，合待朝命，何乃云云，妄生異意！

translations.literal: When Baozhen died, the junior officers Yuan Zhongjing and others discussed installing Baozhen's son Jian; the army was in turmoil. Qianxiu said sternly to the assembly, "Army and prefecture belong to the Son of Heaven; when the commander is absent, we should await the court's command—why all this talk and reckless plotting!
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen died, Yuan Zhongjing and others plotted to install his son Jian, throwing the army into turmoil. Qianxiu said sternly to the troops, "This command belongs to the Son of Heaven. When the commander dies we await the court's orders—why plot rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」軍中服從其言，由是竟免潰亂。

translations.literal: " The army obeyed his words, and thereby was finally spared collapse and riot.
translations.idiomatic: " The army obeyed him, and a full-scale mutiny was averted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知而嘉之，以邕王為昭義節度觀察大使，授虔休潞州左司馬，依前兼御史大夫，掌留後，仍賜名虔休。

translations.literal: The court learned of this and commended him; the Prince of Yong was made grand observation commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, and Qianxiu was appointed Left Administrator of Luzhou, continuing as before as Grand Censor in charge of the acting commission, and was also granted the name Qianxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of this and commended him. The Prince of Yong became grand observation commissioner of Zhaoyi; Qianxiu was appointed left administrator of Luzhou, retained rank as grand censor, took charge as acting commissioner, and was granted the name Qianxiu.

sentences.zh: 號令安撫。

translations.literal: His orders pacified and comforted the people.
translations.idiomatic: His orders brought calm and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 軍州大理。

translations.literal: Army and prefecture were greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Army and prefecture were well governed.

sentences.zh: 二歲，遷潞州長史、昭義軍節度、澤潞磁邢洺觀察使，尋加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to Chief Administrator of Luzhou, military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army, and observation commissioner of Zelu, Ci, Xing, and Ming; shortly afterward he was given the additional post of Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became chief administrator of Luzhou, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and observation commissioner over Zelu, Ci, Xing, and Ming, and soon afterward acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈左僕射，賻以布帛米粟。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director, and condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were given.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days. He was posthumously enfeoffed as left vice director, with gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain.

sentences.zh: 虔休性恭勤，儉省節用，管內州倉庾皆積糧儲，可支軍人數歲。

translations.literal: Qianxiu was by nature respectful and diligent, frugal and economical; in every prefectural granary within his jurisdiction grain was stored in reserve, enough to supply the army for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu was respectful, diligent, and frugal. Granaries throughout his jurisdiction held reserves sufficient to feed the army for years.

sentences.zh: 又嘗撰《誕聖樂曲》以進，其表曰：

translations.literal: He also once composed the "Birth of the Sage" musical piece and presented it; his memorial read:
translations.idiomatic: He also composed a "Birth of the Sage" musical work and presented it with this memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞於師，夫君子為能知樂，是故審音以知聲，審樂以知政，則理道備矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard from his teachers that the gentleman is able to understand music; therefore by examining tones one knows sounds, by examining music one knows government, and then the Way of order is complete.
translations.idiomatic: I have learned from my teachers that the gentleman understands music: by discerning tones one knows sound, by discerning music one knows governance, and thus the way of order is complete.

sentences.zh: 清明廣大，終始周旋，與天地同其和，與四時合其序，豈止於鐘鼓管磬雲乎哉！

translations.literal: Clear and bright, vast and great, turning from beginning to end—it shares harmony with Heaven and Earth and keeps pace with the four seasons; how could it be limited to bells, drums, pipes, and stones alone!
translations.idiomatic: Clear and vast, circling from beginning to end, it harmonizes with Heaven and Earth and keeps pace with the four seasons—far more than bells, drums, pipes, and stones alone!

sentences.zh: 臣伏見開元中天長節著於甲令，每於是日海縣歡娛，稱萬壽之無疆，樂一人之有慶，故能追堯接舜，邁禹逾湯，自周已後，不能議矣。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly observes that in the Kaiyuan era the Heavenly Longevity Festival was recorded in statute; on that day every district within the seas rejoiced, proclaimed boundless longevity, and celebrated the good fortune of the One Man—thereby able to follow Yao and connect with Shun, surpassing Yu and exceeding Tang; since the Zhou none could match it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan the Heavenly Longevity Festival was written into law; on that day the realm rejoiced, hailed boundless longevity, and celebrated the emperor's fortune—rivaling Yao and Shun, surpassing Yu and Tang. Since the Zhou, nothing had equaled it.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以陛下降誕之辰，未有惟新之曲。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to think that for Your Majesty's birth there is as yet no newly composed piece.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for Your Majesty's birthday there is still no new composition.

sentences.zh: 雖太和已佈於六氣，而大樂未宣於八音，無乃臣子之分，或有所闕。

translations.literal: Although the Great Harmony has been spread through the six qi, the Great Music has not yet been proclaimed through the eight sounds—might not the duty of subject and minister be in some measure lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Though great harmony pervades the six qi, the great music has not yet sounded through the eight tones—perhaps we subjects have fallen short in our duty.

sentences.zh: 愚臣不揆頑昧，敢思祖述，每思歌竊抃，忘寢與食久矣。

translations.literal: This foolish servant, without measuring his dullness, dares to think of following the ancients; whenever I think of composing a song I secretly clap my hands and have long forgotten sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy as I am, I have long wished to follow the ancients; whenever I thought of composing a hymn I could scarcely eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 適遇有知音者，與臣論及樂章，探微賾奧，窮理盡性，臣乃遣造《繼天誕聖樂》一曲。

translations.literal: It happened that I met one who understands music; he and I discussed musical pieces, probing the subtle and recondite, exhausting principle and nature, and your servant thereupon had composed the piece "Continuing Heaven's Birth of the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: I recently met a connoisseur of music with whom I discussed composition, probing its deepest principles, and have had composed the piece "Continuing Heaven's Birth of the Sage."

sentences.zh: 大抵以宮為調，表五音之奉君也；

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the gong mode is used as the key, showing how the five tones serve the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Broadly, it uses the gong mode as its key, showing how the five tones serve the ruler;

sentences.zh: 以土為德，知五運之居中也。

translations.literal: earth as the virtue, knowing that among the five cycles earth occupies the center.
translations.idiomatic: and earth as the virtue, knowing that among the five cycles earth occupies the center.

sentences.zh: 凡二十五遍，法二十四氣而足成一歲也。

translations.literal: In all there are twenty-five repetitions, patterned on the twenty-four qi to complete one year.
translations.idiomatic: It has twenty-five repetitions, patterned on the twenty-four qi to complete a full year.

sentences.zh: 每遍一十六拍，象八元、八凱登庸於朝也。

translations.literal: Each repetition has sixteen beats, symbolizing the Eight Primes and Eight Supports taking office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Each repetition has sixteen beats, symbolizing the Eight Primes and Eight Supports taking office at court.

sentences.zh: 所冀《雲門》、《咸池》，永傳於律呂，空桑、孤竹，合薦於宮懸，不聞沾滯之聲，長作中和之樂。

translations.literal: It is hoped that "Yunmen" and "Xianchi" may be transmitted forever in the pitch pipes; the Kongsang and Guzhu may together be offered at the palace bells; no cloying or sluggish sound be heard, but the music of central harmony be made long-lasting.
translations.idiomatic: May "Yunmen" and "Xianchi" endure through the pitch pipes; may the Kongsang and Guzhu instruments join the palace ensemble—no sluggish sound, but lasting music of perfect harmony.

sentences.zh: 可使九域之人，頓忘於肉味；

translations.literal: It can make the people of the nine regions suddenly forget the taste of meat;
translations.idiomatic: It may make the people of the nine regions forget the taste of meat;

sentences.zh: 四夷之俗，皆播於薰風。

translations.literal: the customs of the four barbarians all spread under the balmy breeze.
translations.idiomatic: and spread the customs of the four quarters beneath the balmy breeze.

sentences.zh: 與唐惟休，終古盡善。

translations.literal: With Tang there is only repose; from antiquity to the end, all is goodness.
translations.idiomatic: With Tang there is only repose—goodness perfected for all time.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝懇款屏營之至，謹昧死陳獻以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot overcome his earnest sincerity and trembling anxiety; he respectfully risks death to present this for Your Majesty's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot express my earnest devotion and trembling respect; I humbly risk my life to present this for Your Majesty's hearing.

sentences.zh: 其所造譜，謹同封進。

translations.literal: The score he composed is respectfully enclosed and submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: The score is respectfully enclosed and submitted herewith.

sentences.zh: 先時，有太常樂工劉玠流落至潞州，虔休因令造此曲以進，今《中和樂》起此也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices musician Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu therefore had him compose this piece to present, and today's "Central Harmony Music" arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court musician Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu had him compose this piece for presentation. Today's "Central Harmony Music" originated here.

sentences.zh: 盧從史，其先自元魏已來，冠冕頗盛。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi—his forebears since the Northern Wei had been quite eminent in official caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi's family had held high office since the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父虔，少孤，好學，舉進士，歷御史府三院、刑部郎中、江汝二州刺史、秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Qian was orphaned young, loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served in the three bureaus of the Censorate, as Director in the Ministry of Justice, as Prefect of the two prefectures Jiang and Ru, and as Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian was orphaned young, loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served in the censorate, as director in the Ministry of Justice, as prefect of Jiang and Ru, and as director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 從史少矜力，習騎射，游澤、潞間，節度使李長榮用為大將。

translations.literal: Congshi in youth prided himself on strength, studied riding and archery, wandered between Ze and Lu, and was employed as a great general by military commissioner Li Changrong.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi prided himself on strength as a youth, trained in horsemanship and archery, and wandered between Ze and Lu until Li Changrong employed him as a senior general.

sentences.zh: 德宗中歲，每命節制，必令採訪本軍為其所歸者。

translations.literal: In Dezong's middle years, whenever a military commission was appointed, he always ordered inquiry into whom the native army favored.
translations.idiomatic: In his middle years Dezong always inquired whom the local army favored before appointing a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長榮卒，從史因軍情，且善迎奉中使，得授昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Changrong died, Congshi, relying on army sentiment and being skilled at welcoming palace envoys, received appointment as military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: When Changrong died, Congshi won army support and courted palace envoys skillfully, and was appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 漸狂恣不道，至奪部將妻妾，而辯給矯妄，從事孔戡等以言直不從引去。

translations.literal: He gradually became wildly arrogant and lawless, even seizing the wives and concubines of his subordinate generals; he was glib and deceitful, and his aides Kong Kan and others, because their frank words were not followed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He grew wildly arrogant and lawless, even seizing his officers' wives and concubines. He was glib and deceitful; aides such as Kong Kan left when their frank counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 前年丁父憂，朝旨未議起復，屬王士真卒，從史竊獻誅承宗計，以希上意，用是起授，委其成功。

translations.literal: The year before last he entered mourning for his father; the court had not yet discussed recall from mourning. When Wang Shizhen died, Congshi secretly presented a plan to execute Chengzong to win imperial favor; for this he was recalled and entrusted with success.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier he had entered mourning for his father before the court had considered recall. When Wang Shizhen died, Congshi secretly proposed executing Chengzong to please the throne and was recalled from mourning and entrusted with the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及詔下討賊，兵出，逗留不進，陰與承宗通謀，令軍士潛懷賊號，又高其芻粟之價，售於度支，諷朝廷求宰相；

translations.literal: When the edict to campaign against the rebels was issued and the army marched out, he lingered without advancing, secretly conspired with Chengzong, had soldiers secretly keep rebel titles, also raised the price of fodder and grain and sold it to the fiscal commission, and insinuated to the court that he should be made chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign edict was issued his army marched but lingered without advancing. He conspired secretly with Chengzong, had soldiers keep rebel titles, inflated fodder prices sold to the fiscal commission, and hinted that he should be made chief minister;

sentences.zh: 且誣奏諸軍與賊通，兵不可進。

translations.literal: and also falsely memorialized that the various armies were in communication with the rebels and that the troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: and falsely reported that other armies were colluding with the rebels so that the campaign could not proceed.

sentences.zh: 上深患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 護軍中尉吐突承璀將神策兵與之對壘，從史往往過其營博戲。

translations.literal: Army-protecting eunuch Tutu Chenghui led the Shence troops to face him in camp; Congshi often came to his camp to gamble.
translations.idiomatic: Army-protecting eunuch Tutu Chenghui led the Shence army against him; Congshi often visited his camp to gamble.

sentences.zh: 從史沓貪好得，承璀出寶帶、奇玩以炫燿之，時其愛悅而遺焉，從史喜甚，日益狎。

translations.literal: Congshi was greedy and loved gain; Chenghui produced jeweled belts and rare curios to dazzle him, and from time to time when he was pleased gave them as gifts. Congshi was greatly pleased and grew daily more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi was greedy; Chenghui displayed jeweled belts and rare curios and gave them when pleased. Congshi was delighted and grew more intimate daily.

sentences.zh: 上知其事，取裴垍之謀，因戒承璀伺其來博，揖語，幕下伏壯士，突起，持捽出帳後縛之，內車中，馳以赴闕。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of this and adopted Pei Ji's plan, instructing Chenghui to watch for his coming to gamble, bow and speak with him, with stout men hidden below the tent who would spring up, seize and drag him out behind the tent and bind him, put him in a carriage, and gallop to present him at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted Pei Ji's plan and instructed Chenghui: when Congshi came to gamble, bow and converse with him while stout men hidden beneath the tent would seize him, bind him behind the tent, place him in a carriage, and rush him to court.

sentences.zh: 從者驚亂，斬十數人，余號令乃定，且宣諭密詔，追赴闕庭。

translations.literal: His followers were startled into disorder; more than ten were beheaded before the rest were brought to order by command, and the secret edict was proclaimed urging them to proceed to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: His followers panicked; more than ten were beheaded before order was restored and the secret edict proclaimed, ordering them to proceed to court.

sentences.zh: 都將烏重胤素懷忠順，乃嚴戒其軍，眾不敢動。

translations.literal: Chief commander Wu Zhongyin had long cherished loyalty and obedience; he strictly warned his army, and the troops did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commander Wu Zhongyin, long loyal, strictly restrained his troops, and they did not stir.

sentences.zh: 會夜，使疾驅，未明出境，道路人莫知。

translations.literal: It was night; the envoy drove swiftly; before dawn they left the border, and travelers on the road knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled by night at full speed and crossed the border before dawn; no traveler knew.

sentences.zh: 元和五年四月，制曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuanhe, an edict proclaimed:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanhe 5, an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 邪以蓄眾，自致覆車；

translations.literal: Wickedness amasses followers and brings overturned chariots upon oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Wickedness gathers followers and overturns its own chariot;

sentences.zh: 奸以事君，所宜用鉞。

translations.literal: treachery in serving the ruler deserves the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: treachery toward one's lord deserves the battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 故楚人告變，韓信患釋於事先；

translations.literal: Thus when the men of Chu reported a plot, Han Xin's trouble was resolved beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: When the men of Chu reported a plot, Han Xin's trouble was resolved beforehand;

sentences.zh: 蜀土征災，鐘會禍生於部下。

translations.literal: when Shu campaigned against disaster, Zhong Hui's calamity arose from his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: when Shu campaigned against disaster, Zhong Hui's calamity arose from his own subordinates.

sentences.zh: 況害深楚、蜀，功匪鐘、韓，構此厲階，佈於公議。

translations.literal: How much more when the harm is deeper than in Chu and Shu, the merit unlike that of Zhong or Han—he has built this ladder of calamity, spread through public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when the harm exceeds Chu and Shu, the merit unlike Zhong's or Han's—he has built this ladder of calamity, as public opinion attests.

sentences.zh: 懷私負德，合置於嚴科；

translations.literal: Harbor private ends and betray grace—he should be placed under severe punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Harbor private ends and betray grace—he deserves severe punishment;

sentences.zh: 屈法申恩，尚從於寬典。

translations.literal: yet bending the law to extend favor, we still follow the lenient code.
translations.idiomatic: yet bending the law to show mercy, we still follow the lenient code.

sentences.zh: 前昭義軍節度副大使、知節度事盧從史，擢自裨將，居於大籓，不思報國之誠，每設徇身之計。

translations.literal: Former Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and Acting Commissioner Lu Congshi was promoted from a junior officer and placed in a great frontier commission, yet did not think of loyalty to the state and constantly devised schemes for his own advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Former deputy military commissioner and acting commissioner of Zhaoyi Lu Congshi was promoted from a junior officer to a great frontier post, yet thought not of serving the state and constantly schemed for his own advancement.

sentences.zh: 比丁家禍，曾無戚容，行棄人倫，孝虧大性。

translations.literal: When he recently entered family mourning he showed no grief; in conduct he abandoned human relations and in filial piety failed the great nature.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his father he showed no grief, abandoning human decency and filial duty.

sentences.zh: 屬常山稱亂，朝制未行，固願興師，苟求復位。

translations.literal: When Changshan rose in rebellion and court regulations had not yet been carried out, he firmly wished to raise troops and sought by any means to regain his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Changshan rebelled and court orders had not yet been issued, he eagerly sought to raise troops and regain his post by any means.

sentences.zh: 刻期效用，請以身先；

translations.literal: He set a date for effectiveness and asked to take the lead in person;
translations.idiomatic: He set a deadline for results and asked to lead in person;

sentences.zh: 指日投誠，誓雲獨致。

translations.literal: pointed to a day for submission and swore he alone would achieve it.
translations.idiomatic: pledged submission on a set day and swore he alone would achieve it.

sentences.zh: 示於懷撫，推以信誠。

translations.literal: We showed him comforting favor and extended trust and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: We showed him comforting favor and extended trust and sincerity.

sentences.zh: 排眾論以釋其苴麻，決中心而授之鈇鉞，委以重任，命之專征。

translations.literal: We set aside public debate to release him from his hemp mourning, resolved in our hearts to grant him the battle-axe, entrusted him with heavy responsibility, and ordered him to campaign independently.
translations.idiomatic: We set aside public debate to release him from mourning, resolved in our hearts to grant him command, entrusted him with heavy responsibility, and ordered him to campaign independently.

sentences.zh: 章奏所陳，事無違者；

translations.literal: Whatever he stated in memorials, nothing was refused;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he requested in memorials was granted;

sentences.zh: 恩光是貸，予何愛焉。

translations.literal: favors and grace were lent—what would We withhold?
translations.idiomatic: favors and grace were freely given—what would We withhold?

sentences.zh: 而乃冒利蓄奸，隳政敗度，成師既出，保敵而交通；

translations.literal: Yet he coveted profit and harbored treachery, ruined government and broke regulations; the formed army had marched out, yet he protected the enemy and maintained communication;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he coveted profit and harbored treachery, ruined government and broke regulations; though the army had marched out, he protected the enemy and kept in contact;

sentences.zh: 邪計以行，臨戎而向背。

translations.literal: wicked schemes were carried out, and facing the army he turned back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: wicked schemes were carried out, and facing battle he wavered between loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 諸侯盡力而不應，遺寇遊魂而是托。

translations.literal: The feudal lords exerted all their strength but he did not respond; he entrusted himself to the remnant bandits and wandering rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Other lords exerted all their strength but he did not respond, entrusting himself to remnant rebels.

sentences.zh: 臣節既喪，恩豈念於生成；

translations.literal: Ministerial integrity was already lost—how could he think of the grace that gave him life;
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial duty was abandoned—how could he remember the grace that gave him life;

sentences.zh: 台位於求，禮頓虧於忠敬。

translations.literal: he sought a seat at the council table, and ritual was suddenly diminished in loyalty and respect.
translations.idiomatic: he sought a seat at the council table, and loyalty and respect were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 肆其醜行，熾以凶威，至於逼脅軍中，潛施賊號；

translations.literal: He indulged his ugly conduct and inflamed his fierce authority, even to coercing the army and secretly imposing rebel titles;
translations.idiomatic: He indulged vile conduct and fierce intimidation, even coercing the army and secretly imposing rebel titles;

sentences.zh: 陵污麾下，實玷皇風。

translations.literal: he insulted and defiled those under his command, truly staining the imperial wind.
translations.idiomatic: he insulted and defiled his subordinates, truly staining the imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 貨以籓身，虐而用眾，士庶怨而罔恤，將校勞而不圖。

translations.literal: He used goods to enrich himself, was cruel in employing the masses; soldiers and commoners resented him yet he showed no pity, generals and officers toiled yet he made no plans for them.
translations.idiomatic: He enriched himself with goods, was cruel toward the masses; soldiers and civilians resented him yet he showed no pity, and his officers toiled yet he made no plans for their welfare.

sentences.zh: 稟於陶鈞，行事至此，視於天地，負我何多，且辜覆載之仁，寧逭神鬼之責。

translations.literal: Entrusted by the potter's wheel, his conduct reached this point; viewed before Heaven and Earth, how much he has failed Us—and moreover betrayed the grace that covers and bears all; how could he escape the reckoning of spirits and ghosts?
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted by Heaven's potter's wheel, his conduct reached this point; before Heaven and Earth, how deeply he has failed Us, betrayed the grace that covers all, and cannot escape the reckoning of spirits.

sentences.zh: 況頃年上請，就食山東，及遣旋師，不時恭命，致動其眾，覬生其心，賴劉濟抗忠正之辭，使邪豎絕遲回之計。

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent years he requested to draw provisions from Shandong, and when ordered to withdraw his army he did not promptly obey with respect, stirring his troops and awakening covetous hearts; only thanks to Liu Ji's forthright words of loyalty and rectitude were the wicked halted from their wavering plans.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he recently requested provisions from Shandong, and when ordered to withdraw did not obey promptly, stirring his troops to covetous designs—only Liu Ji's forthright loyal words stopped the wicked from their wavering plans.

sentences.zh: 加以遍毀鄰境，密疏事情，反覆百端，高下萬變，心無恥愧，事至滿盈。

translations.literal: Added to this, he slandered neighboring territories everywhere and sent secret memorials on affairs, changing back and forth in a hundred ways and shifting high and low in ten thousand fashions, with no shame in his heart, until matters reached overflowing fullness.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered neighboring territories and sent secret memorials, shifting position endlessly without shame until his offenses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 朕念以始終，務於含貸，所期悔過，豈謂逾凶。

translations.literal: We considered him from beginning to end and strove for forbearance, expecting repentance—who would have thought he would exceed in wickedness?
translations.idiomatic: We considered him from beginning to end and strove for forbearance, expecting repentance—who would have thought he would grow worse?

sentences.zh: 而昭義軍忠節夙彰，義聲昭著，發其眾怒，葉以一心，顧大惡而不容，幸全軀而自免，宜從大戮，以正彝章。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhaoyi army's loyalty and integrity have long been manifest, its righteous reputation clear; rousing the wrath of the masses, they cast him off with one heart, looking upon his great evil and unable to tolerate it, fortunate to preserve their bodies and escape themselves—they should follow the great execution to rectify the constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhaoyi army's loyalty is long renowned; roused to wrath, they cast him off with one heart, unable to tolerate his great evil and fortunate to preserve themselves—they deserve the supreme penalty to uphold the law.

sentences.zh: 尚以曾列方隅，嘗經任使，惜君臣之體，抑中外之情，俾投魑魅之鄉，以解人神之憤。

translations.literal: Still, because he once held a frontier post and was once entrusted with office, cherishing the form of ruler and minister and restraining feelings within and without, We send him to the land of demons and sprites to release the wrath of men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Still, because he once held frontier office, cherishing the bond between ruler and minister and restraining feelings at court and in the army, We send him to the land of demons to appease the wrath of men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 可貶驩州司馬。

translations.literal: He may be demoted to Prefectural Administrator of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to prefectural administrator of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 奸由事驗，自開棄絕之門；

translations.literal: Treachery is verified by deeds and opens the door to abandonment by oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Treachery is verified by deeds and opens the door to one's own ruin;

sentences.zh: 禍實己招，豈漏恢疏之網。

translations.literal: calamity is truly self-invited—how could it escape the vast and lenient net?
translations.idiomatic: calamity is self-invited—how could it escape the vast net of law?

sentences.zh: 凡百多士，宜諒朕懷。

translations.literal: All you many officers should understand Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: All you officers should understand Our mind.

sentences.zh: 子繼宗等四人並貶嶺外。

translations.literal: His sons Jizong and three others were all demoted beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jizong and three others were all demoted beyond the Ling mountains.

sentences.zh: 李芃，字茂初，趙郡人也。

translations.literal: Li Peng, courtesy name Maochu, was a native of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Peng, courtesy name Maochu, was from Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 解褐上邽主簿，三遷試大理評事，攝監察御史、山南東道觀察支使。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the sackcloth he became Registrar of Shanggui; after three promotions he was made Probationary Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, acting Investigating Censor, and support commissioner of the Southeast Shannan observation circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering service he became registrar of Shanggui; after three promotions he was made probationary assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, acting investigating censor, and support commissioner of Southeast Shannan.

sentences.zh: 嚴武為京兆尹，舉為長安尉。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu was Intendant of the Capital, he recommended Peng as Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu served as intendant of the capital, he recommended Peng for the post of magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李勉為江西觀察使，署奏秘書郎、兼監察御史，為判官。

translations.literal: When Li Mian was Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, he appointed Peng in memorial as Secretary and concurrent Investigating Censor, making him a staff adjudicator.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mian was commissioner of Jiangxi, he recommended Peng for appointment as secretary and concurrent investigating censor, and made him his staff adjudicator.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，轉兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai, he was transferred to concurrent Palace Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongtai era, he was transferred to the concurrent post of palace investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時宣、饒二州人方清、陳莊聚眾據山洞，西絕江路，劫商旅以為亂。

translations.literal: At that time, Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuancheng and Raozhou gathered crowds and held mountain caves, cutting off the river route to the west, and plundering travelers and merchants to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang of Xuancheng and Raozhou rallied bands of men in mountain strongholds, severing the western river route and raiding travelers and merchants in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 芃乃請於秋浦置州，守其要地，以破其謀。

translations.literal: Peng thereupon requested to establish a prefecture at Qiupu to guard the strategic point and break their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Peng then proposed establishing a new prefecture at Qiupu to hold a key position and thwart their plans.

sentences.zh: 李勉然其計，以聞，代宗嘉之，以宣州之秋浦、青陽、饒州之至德置池州焉。

translations.literal: Li Mian approved his plan and reported it; Emperor Daizong commended it, and from Xuancheng's Qiupu and Qingyang and Raozhou's Zhide established Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian endorsed the plan and reported it to the throne. Emperor Daizong approved, and Chizhou was created from Qiupu and Qingyang in Xuancheng and Zhide in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 芃攝行事，無幾，乃兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Peng acted as administrator; before long, he also received concurrent Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Peng served as acting administrator, and before long he was given the concurrent title of attending censor.

sentences.zh: 居無何，魏少游代勉為使，復署奏檢校虞部員外郎，賜金紫，為都團練副使。

translations.literal: Before long had passed, Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian as commissioner; again he memorialized appointment as Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, was granted gold seal and purple robe, and made Deputy Commissioner for Mass Training.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wei Shaoyou succeeded Mian as commissioner. Peng was again recommended as acting vice director of the Ministry of Works, granted the gold seal and purple robe, and made deputy commissioner for mass training.

sentences.zh: 頃之，攝江州刺史，州人便之。

translations.literal: Before long, he acted as Prefect of Jiangzhou; the people of the prefecture found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was acting prefect of Jiangzhou, to the great benefit of the people there.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，免喪，永平軍節度李勉署奏檢校工部郎中、兼侍御史，為判官，尋攝陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Observing mourning for his mother, upon completion of mourning Li Mian, Military Governor of Yongping Army, memorialized appointment as Acting Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Attending Censor, as staff adjudicator; soon he acted as Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his mother and completing the period of mourning, Li Mian, military governor of Yongping Army, recommended him as acting director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent attending censor on his staff. Before long he was acting prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲中，即值李靈曜反於汴州，勉署芃兼亳州防禦使，練達軍事，兵備甚肅；

translations.literal: Within the year, it happened that Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou; Mian appointed Peng concurrent Defender of Bozhou; skilled in military affairs, his armaments were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou. Mian appointed Peng concurrent defender of Bozhou. Experienced in military affairs, he maintained the troops in excellent readiness.

sentences.zh: 又開陳、潁運路，以通漕輓。

translations.literal: He also opened the transport route through Chen and Ying to connect grain convoys.
translations.idiomatic: He also reopened the transport route through Chen and Ying to restore the grain supply lines.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，授檢校太常少卿、兼御史中丞、河陽三城鎮遏使。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrent Vice Censor in Chief, and Suppression Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, Peng was appointed acting vice minister of rites, concurrent vice censor in chief, and suppression commissioner of the three cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 撫勞備至，資廩善者，必先軍士。

translations.literal: In comforting and rewarding he was thorough; whenever provisions in the stores were good, soldiers always came first.
translations.idiomatic: He was scrupulous in comforting and rewarding his men, and whenever the stores held good provisions, the soldiers always received them first.

sentences.zh: 間一年，為節度使路嗣恭之副，加檢校左庶子、河陽三城懷州節度觀察使，以東畿汜水等五縣隸焉。
