translations.literal: After a year, he became deputy to Military Governor Lu Sigong; added Acting Left Household Companion, Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang and Huaizhou; the five counties of Sishui and others in the eastern capital area were placed under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became deputy to Military Governor Lu Sigong and was given the additional titles of acting left household companion and military governor and observation commissioner of the three cities of Heyang and Huaizhou, with five counties including Sishui in the eastern capital region placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 時河南北連大兵，詔益以神策、汝、陝之師。

translations.literal: At that time great armies were engaged continuously north and south of the Yellow River; an edict added the Shence Army and troops from Ru and Shan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At that time major campaigns were underway on both sides of the Yellow River, and an imperial edict reinforced him with the Shence Army and troops from Ru and Shan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 芃進收新鄉、共城，遂圍衛州。

translations.literal: Peng advanced to recover Xinxiang and Gongcheng, then besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng advanced and retook Xinxiang and Gongcheng, then laid siege to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔與河東節度馬燧等諸軍破田悅於洹水，以功加檢校兵部尚書，累封開郡王，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict ordered him with Hedong Military Governor Ma Sui and other armies to defeat Tian Yue at Huanshui; for merit he was added Acting Minister of War, successively enfeoffed as Prince of Kai commandery, with a fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was ordered to join Military Governor Ma Sui of Hedong and other forces in defeating Tian Yue at Huanshui. For his achievements he was promoted to acting minister of war, enfeoffed successively as Prince of Kai commandery, with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進圍悅於魏州，將符璘以精騎五百夜降，芃耳開營以納之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Yue at Weizhou, the general Fu Lin with five hundred elite horsemen surrendered by night; Peng personally opened the camp to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege of Tian Yue at Weizhou continued, General Fu Lin came over by night with five hundred elite cavalry. Peng personally opened the camp to admit them.

sentences.zh: 明日，歸璘於招討使。

translations.literal: The next day, he returned Lin to the Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned Fu Lin to the pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上居奉天，斂軍還。

translations.literal: The emperor resided at Fengtian; Peng gathered the army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Fengtian, Peng withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 興元初，檢校右僕射，無何，以疾固讓罷歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan, he was made Acting Right Vice Director; before long, on account of illness he firmly declined and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era he was made acting right vice director, but before long, citing illness, he steadfastly declined the post and was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 芃將請告，謂所親曰：「今年夏被蝗旱，人主厭兵革，然則天下城壘堅厚矣，戈鋋銛利矣，以力勝之，則有得失，其可盡乎！

translations.literal: When Peng was about to request leave, he said to those close to him: "This summer there were locusts and drought; the sovereign is weary of war—yet throughout the realm city walls and ramparts are thick and strong, and spears and blades are sharp. To overcome by force brings gains and losses. Can such a course be taken to the end?"
translations.idiomatic: When Peng was about to request leave, he told those close to him: "This summer brought locusts and drought, and the sovereign is weary of war. Yet throughout the realm the walls and ramparts have grown thick and strong, and spears and blades sharper than ever. Victory by force alone brings as many losses as gains. Can we truly see such a course through to the end?"

sentences.zh: 除弊之急，莫先德化，循而理之，斯易致耳。

translations.literal: In urgently removing ills, nothing comes before transforming through virtue; managing things by steady progress—this is easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The most urgent task is to remove abuses, and nothing should come before moral transformation. Govern steadily and patiently, and success will come easily.

sentences.zh: 方鎮之戴翼時主，宜先退讓，貪權持祿，吾所不取也。

translations.literal: Regional commanders who shelter the ruler with outspread wings should first yield and step back; to clutch power and hold salary—this I will not accept.
translations.idiomatic: A regional commander who supports the throne should know when to yield. Clinging to power and salary for their own sake is something I will not do.

sentences.zh: 吾既疾病，豈能言而不踐乎！

translations.literal: I am already ill—how can I speak and not act on it!
translations.idiomatic: I am already ill—how can I speak these words and then not live by them!

sentences.zh: 」乃手疏乞罷。

translations.literal: Then he wrote a memorial by hand requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a personal memorial requesting to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年卒，年六十四，廢朝一日，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he died, age sixty-four; the court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously appointed him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhenyuan, at the age of sixty-four. The court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously appointed him grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李澄，遼東襄平人，隋蒲山公寬之後也，居京兆。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, was a descendant of Kuanshan Duke Kuan of Sui; he lived in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was from Xiangping in Liaodong and a descendant of Duke Kuan of Kuanshan in the Sui dynasty; his family settled in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父鎬，清江太守，以澄贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Hao was Prefect of Qingjiang; because of Cheng he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao had been prefect of Qingjiang; because of Cheng's status, Hao was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 澄以武藝為偏將，累除試將作監，隸於江淮都統李峘。

translations.literal: Cheng, by martial skill, became a deputy general; repeatedly removed and made Probationary Director of Imperial Construction, he was subordinate to Li Chan, overall commander of the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng entered service as a deputy general on the strength of his martial skill and was repeatedly promoted to probationary director of imperial construction, serving under Li Chan, overall commander of the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 建中初，以檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞隸於永平軍節度使李勉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, as Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor in Chief he was subordinate to Li Mian, Military Governor of Yongping Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he served under Li Mian, military governor of Yongping Army, with the titles of acting guest of the heir apparent and concurrent vice censor in chief.

sentences.zh: 及勉移理汴州，乃奏澄為滑州刺史。

translations.literal: When Mian transferred administration to Bianzhou, he then memorialized Cheng as Prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian moved his headquarters to Bianzhou, he recommended Cheng for appointment as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，李希烈陷汴州，勉奔歸行在，澄遂以城降希烈，偽署尚書令，兼滑州永平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, Li Xilie captured Bianzhou; Mian fled back to the mobile court, and Cheng thereupon surrendered the city to Xilie; falsely appointed Chancellor and concurrent Military Governor of Yongping Army at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year, Li Xilie took Bianzhou. Mian fled to the mobile court, and Cheng surrendered the city to Xilie, who falsely appointed him chancellor and concurrent military governor of Yongping Army at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年春，澄密令親信人盧融間道賚表達於奉天，上嘉之，乃以帛詔藏於蠟丸中，加澄刑部尚書，兼汴州刺史、汴滑節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng secretly sent his trusted man Lu Rong by a hidden route bearing a memorial to Fengtian; the emperor commended it, and placed an edict written on silk within a wax pellet, appointing Cheng Minister of Justice, concurrent Prefect of Bianzhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Bian and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng secretly sent his trusted agent Lu Rong by a hidden route with a memorial to Fengtian. The emperor was pleased and sent back an edict written on silk sealed in a wax pellet, appointing Cheng minister of justice, concurrent prefect of Bianzhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Bian and Hua.

sentences.zh: 澄秘而未宣，乃集州兵嚴加訓習。

translations.literal: Cheng kept it secret and did not announce it; he then gathered the prefectural troops and strictly drilled them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng kept the edict secret and began to muster and rigorously drill the prefectural troops.

sentences.zh: 希烈頗疑之，乃令養子六百人戍之，以虞其變。

translations.literal: Xilie was quite suspicious; he then ordered six hundred adopted sons to garrison there to guard against any change.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie grew suspicious and posted six hundred of his adopted sons as a garrison to guard against any defection.

sentences.zh: 希烈苦攻寧陵，邀澄率其眾至石柱。

translations.literal: Xilie strenuously attacked Ningling and summoned Cheng to lead his crowd to Shizhu.
translations.idiomatic: While Xilie was pressing hard against Ningling, he summoned Cheng to bring his forces to Shizhu.

sentences.zh: 澄令縱火焚營，而偽遁，誘六百人因驚行剽而加其罪，果大俘掠，悉令斬之以告。

translations.literal: Cheng ordered fire set to burn the camp and feigned flight; he lured the six hundred men, and when startled they plundered, he added the crime to them; indeed they looted greatly; he ordered all beheaded and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had his camp set ablaze and staged a false retreat. When the six hundred men panicked and began looting, he used this as grounds against them, had them all executed, and reported the killings to Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈不能窮詰焉。

translations.literal: Xilie could not thoroughly investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was unable to pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 無凡，希烈遣其將翟暉等寇陳州，久之未復。

translations.literal: Before long, Xilie dispatched his generals Zhai Hui and others to raid Chenzhou; for a long time they did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xilie sent his generals Zhai Hui and others to attack Chenzhou, and they were away for a long time.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，澄以汴州兵寡，度希烈不能制己，又會中官薛盈珍持節且至，加檢校兵部尚書，封武威郡王，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, Cheng because Bianzhou had few troops, estimated that Xilie could not control him; it also happened that the palace eunuch Xue Yingzhen was bearing credentials and about to arrive; he was added Acting Minister of War, enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei commandery, granted a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, Cheng calculated that with Bianzhou's small garrison Xilie could no longer control him. At the same time the palace eunuch Xue Yingzhen was approaching with imperial credentials, appointing him acting minister of war, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wuwei commandery, and granting a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 澄乃乘勢力焚賊旌節，誓眾歸國。

translations.literal: Cheng then took advantage of momentum, burned the rebel banners and credentials, and swore the crowd to return to the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the moment, Cheng burned the rebel banners and standards and rallied his men with an oath to return to the imperial cause.

sentences.zh: 及十一月，希烈既失澄，又聞翟暉大敗，由是奔歸蔡州。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month, Xilie having lost Cheng and also hearing that Zhai Hui was greatly defeated, on this account fled back to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By November, Xilie had lost Cheng's support and learned that Zhai Hui had suffered a crushing defeat, and so he fled back to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 澄遽率眾將復汴州，屯於城北門，恇怯不敢進。

translations.literal: Cheng hastily led the crowd intending to recover Bianzhou, encamped at the north city gate, but timidly did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng hurriedly led his forces to retake Bianzhou and encamped at the north gate, but fear held him back from entering the city.

sentences.zh: 及宣武軍節度使劉洽師至城東門，賊將田懷珍開關以納之。

translations.literal: When Military Governor Liu Qia of Xuanwu Army's forces reached the east city gate, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the pass to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qia, military governor of Xuanwu Army, arrived at the east gate, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the gate to admit him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，澄方自北入，洽已據子城。

translations.literal: The next day, Cheng only then entered from the north; Qia had already occupied the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cheng finally entered from the north, but Liu Qia had already taken the inner city.

sentences.zh: 澄乃舍於浚儀縣，兩軍將士，日有忿競，不自安。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon lodged in Junyi county; officers and soldiers of the two armies daily had angry disputes; he was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng withdrew to Junyi county, where officers and soldiers of the two armies clashed daily in angry disputes; he lived in constant unease.

sentences.zh: 會鄭州賊將孫液通款於澄，澄遣其子清赴之。

translations.literal: It happened that the rebel general Sun Ye of Zhengzhou communicated surrender to Cheng; Cheng sent his son Qing to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general Sun Ye of Zhengzhou offered to surrender to Cheng, Cheng sent his son Qing to accept.

sentences.zh: 先是，河陽軍節度使李芃遣其將雍顥攻鄭州，顥所過縱掠，液拒之尤固；

translations.literal: Before this, Li Peng, Military Governor of Heyang Army, sent his general Yong Hao to attack Zhengzhou; wherever Hao passed he indulged in plunder, and Ye resisted him especially firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Peng, military governor of Heyang Army, had sent his general Yong Hao to attack Zhengzhou. Hao had plundered wherever he marched, and Sun Ye had resisted him all the more stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 及清至，遂納之。

translations.literal: When Qing arrived, he thereupon accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing arrived, Sun Ye surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 顥怒攻液，清以眾助之，殺登城者數十人，顥方引退，又焚陽武而歸。

translations.literal: Hao angrily attacked Ye; Qing with his crowd aided him, killed several tens who climbed the walls; Hao only then withdrew, and again burned Yangwu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Hao attacked Sun Ye, but Qing brought his forces to assist and killed dozens of Hao's men who scaled the walls. Hao finally withdrew, burning Yangwu on his way back.

sentences.zh: 澄乃出赴鄭州，朝廷特授清檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞，更名克寧。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon went out to proceed to Zhengzhou; the court specially appointed Qing Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor in Chief, renaming him Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then went to take charge at Zhengzhou. The court specially appointed Qing acting guest of the heir apparent and concurrent vice censor in chief, and gave him the new name Kening.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年三月，就加澄檢校左僕射、義成軍鄭滑許等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhenyuan, Cheng was added on the spot as Acting Left Vice Director and Military Governor of Yicheng Army, Zheng, Hua, Xu and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Zhenyuan, Cheng was promoted on the spot to acting left vice director and military governor of Yicheng Army over Zheng, Hua, Xu, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年五十四，廢朝一日，贈司空，賵布帛粟有差，仍令左散騎常侍歸崇敬充弔祭使，所緣喪葬，並勒官給。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, age fifty-four; audiences suspended one day; posthumously appointed Minister of Works; condolence gifts of cloth, silk, and grain varied; additionally ordered Left Regular Attendant Guichongjing to serve as condolence envoy; all funeral expenses along the route were mandated as official provision.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year, at the age of fifty-four. The court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously appointed him minister of works, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain. The left regular attendant Guichongjing was sent as condolence envoy, and all funeral expenses along the route were to be paid by the state.

sentences.zh: 澄實以八月癸未終，克寧秘之，以九月庚寅，欲自起視事。

translations.literal: Cheng actually ended on the day guiwei in the eighth month; Kening kept it secret; on the day gengyin in the ninth month, he wished to rise himself and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had actually died on guiwei day in the eighth month, but Kening concealed the death. On gengyin day in the ninth month he intended to take office himself.

sentences.zh: 其行軍司馬馬鉉不許，克寧陰遣殺之，乃墨絰而出，加卒於城門，將為不順。

translations.literal: His campaigning staff officer Ma Xuan did not permit it; Kening secretly sent men to kill him; then wearing black mourning headcloth he went out, placing extra guards at the city gates, intending rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His campaigning staff officer Ma Xuan objected, so Kening secretly had him killed. Kening then appeared in black mourning garb, posted additional troops at the city gates, and prepared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 劉洽出師屯於境上以制之，且使告諭切至，由是克寧不敢妄發，然道路絕商旅者凡十四五日。

translations.literal: Liu Qia marched out troops and encamped on the border to control him, and also sent emissaries with stern notices; on this account Kening did not dare rashly act, yet travelers and merchants were cut off on the roads for altogether fourteen or fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia marched troops to the border to restrain him and sent emissaries with stern warnings. Kening did not dare act rashly, but travel and trade were suspended for fourteen or fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 及賈躭代澄，克寧護喪將歸，乃悉索府中財貨，以夜出城，軍人從而剽奪，及明殆盡。

translations.literal: When Jia Dan replaced Cheng, Kening escorting the coffin was about to return; he then entirely seized the goods and wealth in the prefectural office, exiting the city by night; soldiers followed and plundered; by dawn it was nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Dan succeeded Cheng, Kening prepared to escort the coffin home. He seized all the wealth in the prefectural treasury and tried to smuggle it out by night, but soldiers followed and looted until by dawn almost nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 澄柩至京師，又賜克寧莊一所、錢千貫、粟麥二千石。

translations.literal: When Cheng's bier reached the capital, Kening was again granted one estate, one thousand strings of cash, and two thousand piculs of millet and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng's coffin reached the capital, the court also granted Kening an estate, one thousand strings of cash, and two thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 澄初封隴西郡公，進武威郡王，每上疏連稱二封，頗為時人所哂。

translations.literal: Cheng was initially enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery, advanced to Prince of Wuwei commandery; each time he memorialized he linked and used both titles—a matter much ridiculed by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had first been enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery and later promoted to Prince of Wuwei commandery, yet in every memorial he listed both titles together—a habit that people of the time found laughable.

sentences.zh: 李元素，字大朴，蒲山公密之孫。

translations.literal: Li Yuansu, courtesy name Dapu, was grandson of Kuanshan Duke Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuansu, courtesy name Dapu, was a grandson of Duke Mi of Kuanshan.

sentences.zh: 任侍御史，時杜亞為東都留守，惡大將令狐運，會盜發洛城之北，運適與其部下畋於北郊，亞意其為盜，遂執訊之，逮系者四十餘人。

translations.literal: Serving as Attending Censor, at that time Du Ya was Eastern Capital Regent; he hated the great general Linghu Yun; it happened that graves were robbed north of Luoyang city; Yun happened with his subordinates to hunt in the northern suburbs; Ya suspected them as the robbers, then arrested and interrogated them; over forty persons were seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as attending censor, Du Ya was regent of the eastern capital and bore a grudge against the senior general Linghu Yun. When tombs were robbed north of Luoyang, Yun happened to be hunting in the northern suburbs with his men. Du Ya assumed they were the culprits, had them arrested and interrogated, and more than forty people were detained.

sentences.zh: 監察御史楊寧按其事，亞以為不直，密表陳之，寧遂得罪。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Yang Ning reviewed the case; Ya deemed it unjust and secretly memorialized about it; Ning thereupon was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Yang Ning looked into the matter, but Du Ya considered his findings biased and secretly memorialized against him. Yang Ning was punished as a result.

sentences.zh: 亞將逞其宿怒，且以得賊為功，上表指明運為盜之狀，上信而不疑。

translations.literal: Ya was about to vent his old anger, and moreover to take catching the robbers as merit; he memorialized clearly stating Yun's appearance as robber; the emperor believed without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya was eager to vent his long-standing anger and claim credit for catching the culprits. He memorialized, explicitly accusing Linghu Yun of robbery, and the emperor believed him without question.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以獄大宜審，奏請覆之，命元素就決，亞迎路以獄成告。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, because the case was great, deemed it proper to examine carefully; memorialized requesting review; ordered Yuansu to go decide; Ya met him on the road announcing the case already concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers felt a case of this magnitude required careful review and requested a reinvestigation. Yuansu was sent to adjudicate, but Du Ya met him on the road and declared the case already closed.

sentences.zh: 元素驗之五日，盡釋其囚以還。

translations.literal: Yuansu verified for five days, entirely releasing the prisoners and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu reinvestigated for five days and released every prisoner.

sentences.zh: 亞大驚，且怒，親追送，馬上責之，元素不答。

translations.literal: Ya greatly startled, and also angry, personally chased after him; on horseback he rebuked him; Yuansu did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya was astonished and furious. He rode after Yuansu in person and berated him from horseback, but Yuansu made no reply.

sentences.zh: 亞遂上疏，又誣元素。

translations.literal: Ya thereupon memorialized, again slandering Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya then memorialized again, slandering Yuansu.

sentences.zh: 元素還奏，言未畢，上怒曰：「出俟命。

translations.literal: Yuansu returned to memorialize; words not finished, the emperor angrily said: "Go out and await orders."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuansu reported back to the throne, before he could finish the emperor snapped: "Leave and await my orders."

sentences.zh: 」元素曰：「臣未盡詞。

translations.literal: Yuansu said: "Your servant has not finished speaking."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu said: "I have not finished speaking, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」上又曰：「且去」。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "Go for now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said again: "Go for now."

sentences.zh: 元素復奏曰：「一出不得復見陛下，乞容盡詞。

translations.literal: Yuansu again memorialized: "Once I go out I cannot again see Your Majesty; I beg leave to finish my words."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu persisted: "If I leave now I may never see Your Majesty again. I beg you to let me finish."

sentences.zh: 」上意稍緩，元素盡言運冤狀明白，上乃寤曰：「非卿，孰能辨之！

translations.literal: The emperor's mind slightly softened; Yuansu fully stated Yun's wrongful appearance clearly; the emperor then awakened and said: "If not for you, who could distinguish it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger softened. Yuansu laid out Linghu Yun's innocence clearly, and the emperor came to his senses: "Without you, who could have seen through this?"

sentences.zh: 」後數月，竟得其真賊，元素由是為時器重，遷給事中。

translations.literal: After several months, they finally got the true robbers; Yuansu on this account was valued by people of the time, transferred to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the real culprits were caught, and Yuansu came to be highly regarded. He was promoted to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 時美官缺，必指元素。

translations.literal: When prestigious offices were vacant, they always named Yuansu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prestigious office fell vacant, people would mention Yuansu.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant minister of the court of imperial appointments.

sentences.zh: 數月，鄭滑節度盧群卒，遂命元素兼御史大夫，鎮鄭滑，就加檢校工部尚書，在鎮稱理。

translations.literal: After several months, Zheng-Hua Military Governor Lu Qun died; then ordered Yuansu concurrent Censor in Chief, to garrison Zheng and Hua; added on the spot Acting Minister of Works; at his post he was called well-governed.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Lu Qun, military governor of Zheng and Hua, died. Yuansu was appointed concurrent censor in chief and sent to govern Zheng and Hua, promoted on the spot to acting minister of works. His administration earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 元和初，征拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, summoned and appointed Censor in Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he was summoned and appointed censor in chief.

sentences.zh: 自貞元中位缺，久難其人，至是元素以名望召拜，中外聳聽。

translations.literal: Since Zhenyuan the post had been vacant, long difficult to find the man; at this time Yuansu by reputation was summoned and appointed; inside and outside the court listened with raised attention.
translations.idiomatic: The office had been vacant since the Zhenyuan era, and for years no suitable candidate had been found. When Yuansu was summoned by virtue of his reputation, the entire court watched with keen anticipation.

sentences.zh: 及居位，一無修舉，但規求作相。

translations.literal: When he occupied the post, not one improvement or initiative; only schemed seeking to become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he accomplished nothing at all and devoted himself solely to scheming for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 久之，浸不得志，見客必曰：「無以某官散相疏也。

translations.literal: Before long, gradually not getting his wish, meeting guests he always said: "Do not take an official's post lightly and estrange the chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: As time passed and his ambitions remained unfulfilled, he would tell every visitor: "Do not let a mere official title come between you and the chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」見屬官必先拜，脂韋在列，大失人情。

translations.literal: Meeting subordinate officials he always bowed first; fawning and soft behavior was in the ranks; greatly lost people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He would bow first to his own subordinates, and his obsequious, unctuous manner alienated everyone.

sentences.zh: 李錡為亂江南，遂授元素浙西道節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Li Qi rebelled in Jiangnan; thereupon Yuansu was appointed Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of the Zhexi circuit and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi rebelled in Jiangnan, Yuansu was appointed military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Zhexi circuit.

sentences.zh: 數月受代，入拜國子祭酒，尋遷太常卿，轉戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: After several months he was relieved; entered and appointed Grand Master of the National University; soon transferred to Minister of Rites; shifted to Minister of Revenue, adjudicating fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was replaced. He returned to the capital as grand master of the national university, was soon made minister of rites, and then transferred to minister of revenue with responsibility for fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 元素少孤，奉長姊友敬加於人，及其姊歿，沉悲遘疾，上疏懇辭，從之。

translations.literal: Yuansu was orphaned young; toward his elder sister his friendship and respect exceeded others; when his sister died, deeply grieved he fell ill; memorialized earnestly requesting leave; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu lost his parents young and treated his elder sister with exceptional devotion and respect. When she died he was stricken with grief and illness and memorialized for leave, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 數月，以出妻免官。

translations.literal: After several months, for dismissing his wife he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was dismissed from office for divorcing his wife.

sentences.zh: 初，元素再娶妻王氏，石泉公方慶之孫，性柔弱，元素為郎官時娶之，甚禮重，及貴，溺情僕妾，遂薄之。

translations.literal: At first, Yuansu married again Lady Wang, granddaughter of Duke Fangqing of Shiquan; nature gentle and soft; when Yuansu was a Bureau Director he married her, greatly honoring her; when he became noble, indulged affections with servant concubines, then treated her lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu had taken as his second wife Lady Wang, granddaughter of Duke Fangqing of Shiquan, a woman of gentle disposition. He had married her while still a mid-level official and treated her with great respect, but once he rose to high rank he doted on servant concubines and grew cold toward her.

sentences.zh: 且又無子，而前妻之子已長，無良，元素寢疾昏惑，聽譖遂出之，給與非厚。

translations.literal: Moreover she had no son, while the son of the former wife was already grown, without virtue; Yuansu bedridden delirious, listened to slanders and then dismissed her; provisions given were not generous.
translations.idiomatic: She bore him no children, while the son of his first wife had grown into a worthless man. Yuansu, ill and confused in bed, heeded slanderous talk and divorced her, granting her a meager settlement.

sentences.zh: 妻族上訴，乃詔曰：「李元素病中上表，懇切披陳，雲『妻王氏，禮義殊乖，願與離絕』。

translations.literal: The wife's clan appealed upward; then an edict said: "Li Yuansu while ill memorialized, earnestly setting forth, saying 'Wife Wang, ritual and righteousness greatly at variance, I wish to separate and cut off.'"
translations.idiomatic: Her family appealed to the throne, and an edict was issued: "Li Yuansu submitted a memorial while ill, earnestly stating that his wife Lady Wang had gravely violated the norms of ritual and righteousness and that he wished to divorce her."

sentences.zh: 初謂素有醜行，不能顯言，以其大官之家，所以令自處置。

translations.literal: At first it was thought he had long had shameful conduct, which could not be stated openly; because she came from a great official family, he was therefore allowed to dispose of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first we assumed he had serious grounds he could not state openly, and because she came from a distinguished official family, we allowed him to handle the matter himself.

sentences.zh: 訪聞不曾告報妻族，亦無明過可書，蓋是中情不和，遂至於此。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was learned he had never notified the wife's clan, nor were there clear faults that could be written; probably inner feelings were not harmonious, and thus it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed he had never informed her family, nor was there any documented misconduct on her part. Apparently the two had simply fallen out, and matters had come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 脅以王命，當日遣歸，給送之間，又至單薄。

translations.literal: Coerced by imperial command, sent back the same day; in the provisions for sending her off, again it reached meagerness.
translations.idiomatic: She was sent away the same day under imperial pressure, and even the settlement provided for her was miserably small.

sentences.zh: 不唯王氏受辱，實亦朝情悉驚。

translations.literal: Not only did Lady Wang suffer humiliation; in truth the sentiment of the court was entirely shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was not the only one shamed—the entire court was appalled.

sentences.zh: 如此理家，合當懲責。

translations.literal: To manage the household thus—properly ought to be punished and reproved.
translations.idiomatic: Household affairs handled in this manner deserve punishment.

sentences.zh: 宜停官，仍令與王氏錢物，通所奏數滿五千貫。

translations.literal: He should be suspended from office; still ordered to give Lady Wang money and goods, totaling the memorialized amount up to five thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be removed from office and ordered to pay Lady Wang a total of five thousand strings of cash in compensation.

sentences.zh: 」元和五年卒，贈陝州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he died; posthumously appointed Great Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Yuanhe and was posthumously appointed great governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李抱玉、李抱真，以武勇之材，兼忠義之行，有唐之良將也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen, with martial valor as material, together with loyal righteousness in conduct—were good generals of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen combined martial valor with loyal righteousness—they were among the Tang dynasty's finest generals.

sentences.zh: 且如農隙教潞人之射，數騎入武俊之營，非有奇謀，孰能如是。

translations.literal: Moreover, like teaching the people of Lu archery in the intervals of farming, or entering Wu Jun's camp with several horsemen—without extraordinary stratagem, who could be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Consider teaching the people of Lu archery in the farming off-season, or riding into Wang Wujun's camp with only a handful of men—without extraordinary daring and cunning, who could accomplish such things?

sentences.zh: 惜乎服食求仙，為藥所誤。

translations.literal: Alas, ingesting medicines seeking immortality—was misled by elixirs.
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity that in seeking immortality through elixirs, they were undone by the very drugs they consumed.

sentences.zh: 王虔休不黨僭命，有足可嘉；

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu did not side with usurpers; he is fully worthy of praise;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu refused to join the rebels and deserves full praise;

sentences.zh: 盧從史動多懷奸，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi in his movements often harbored treachery and brought calamity upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi was habitually treacherous and brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 芃則老也知足，澄則過而改圖。

translations.literal: Peng in old age knew contentment; Cheng, having erred, changed his course.
translations.idiomatic: Peng in his later years knew when to be satisfied; Cheng, after his mistake, changed course.

sentences.zh: 元素為御史時，執德不回；

translations.literal: When Yuansu was a censor, he held to virtue and would not bend;
translations.idiomatic: As a censor, Yuansu held firm to principle and would not bend;

sentences.zh: 居大夫日，其心甚短。

translations.literal: when he held the post of grand censor, his heart was very small-minded.
translations.idiomatic: but as grand censor his ambitions were petty.

sentences.zh: 因緣七出，益露醜聲，善少惡多，又何足算。

translations.literal: Because of the seven grounds for divorce, his ugly reputation was further exposed; good was few and evil many—what is there to reckon?
translations.idiomatic: His divorce scandal exposed his shame; virtues were few and faults many—little remains worth counting.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：抱玉、抱真，我朝良將。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Baoyu and Baozhen—good generals of our dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Baoyu and Baozhen were fine generals of our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 虔休之心，亦多可尚。

translations.literal: Qianxiu's heart, too, has much to be admired.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu's conduct, too, offers much to admire.

sentences.zh: 史懷奸謀，芃將祿讓。

translations.literal: Congshi harbored treacherous schemes; Peng was about to yield salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi harbored treachery; Peng was ready to yield rank and emolument.

sentences.zh: 澄迷卻行，素貪一響。

translations.literal: Cheng was deluded then turned back; Yuansu was always greedy for the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng strayed, then reversed course; Yuansu was ever greedy for the premiership.

sentences.zh: 吾誰與欺，豈如忠諒。

translations.literal: Whom can We deceive—how could it compare to loyal sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Whom can the throne deceive—how could such men compare to the loyal and sincere?
